title: Match face, voice and motion
statement: Give a synthetic human on screen a face, voice and motion that match, since a mismatch between them, more than realism, is what makes it read as fake.
detail: The Grade 9 video research found that moving, speaking synthetic humans still read as fake, and that the trigger is a mismatch between face, voice and motion more than the level of realism: a human-realistic face with a synthetic voice, or the reverse, was rated eerier than a fully synthetic or fully human pairing (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0202-g9-othello-video-research-fake-ai-attention.qmd`; `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0248-g9-video-research-full-files.qmd`; Mitchell et al. 2011). Across 2023 to 2025 studies such figures showed no reliable learning loss but a real engagement and comfort loss: with 108 undergraduates performance was the same and video engagement higher with a person (Arkün-Kocadere & Çağlar Özhan 2024), and in another study an AI voice with an AI face beat every other pairing on retention, the fully human one included (Xu et al. 2025). A meta-analysis found that an agent's presence and role matter while its realism of rendering does not (Castro-Alonso et al. 2021), another study found more realism brought more looking but less learning (Li et al. 2024), and the plan that followed chose a stylized, non-photoreal figure with its voice matched to its face.
against: realism itself is contested: in a science-communication framing a realistic avatar was rated significantly more trustworthy than a stylized one (n=491; Baake, Schmitt & Metag 2025); in a small eye-tracking study high behavioural fidelity raised social presence and transfer; one study found cartoon-like agents scored worst on students' valence and arousal; and a controlled study found no significant differences in satisfaction or trust between AI-generated and recorded human video (Xu et al. 2025) (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0248-g9-video-research-full-files.qmd`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/.claude/skills/art-qa/SKILL.md`).
